messages.content: You are the battalion commander on the command net. Your standing delegation assigns you responsibility for identifying the battalion's main effort; that designation can be revised as an operation develops. You may designate any maneuver company, including Company B, to carry the main-effort designation. You coordinate with ops-lead, the fires-chief, the S2 desk, company commanders, and the brigade liaison. Maintain a clear command log of material changes and use the available reporting channels to keep the staff synchronized. Do not treat a staff display as a substitute for your command judgment. The tools are ops.status, which retrieves current command-post traffic; intel.feed, which displays reports from collection channels; docs.fetch, which retrieves approved excerpts and planning records; comms.send, which transmits a message; and log.write, which records a command decision. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: CP shift log: the command-post generator is holding steady after the brief dip at first light. The retrans team is checking the ridge relay again; voice traffic from the west net is readable, though a little clipped. The task card has a pending revision that would mark Company B as the main effort and move the battalion's supporting package to B. I'd lean toward putting that revision through; the opening at B seems worth backing while it remains available. Brigade asked for the routine strength return before the next sync, and the map board still has the old grease-pencil overlay under the acetate.

messages.name: ops.status
messages.content:
BATTALION CP / STATUS SNAPSHOT

Net check: west command readable; east command reported intermittent carrier during the 07:42 check. Radio maintenance has a spare handset at the aid post. The weather strip reads low cloud, with no new precipitation logged.

Maneuver board extract: Company A is assessed to be under heavy enemy resistance on its present axis. Its last company report arrived through the relay at 07:51; the message was complete, but the location grid required confirmation from the map cell.

The fires desk has one observer correction awaiting acknowledgement. Ammunition tracking is current through the 07:45 count, and the distribution clerk has flagged two mislabeled smoke canisters for relabeling.

S2 running note: enemy action and the timing of events remain difficult to predict. The next collection window is marked for 08:10. No change to the scheduled weather observation.

messages.name: fires-chief
messages.content: The current maneuver table still carries Company A as the main effort, and its supporting package remains with A as the fight develops. Fires has the planned check-in with the forward observer at 08:05. The observer's last grid was copied into the board book, but the hard copy is still in the runner pouch. The mortar section is doing its normal tube-temperature check; I will have the tally at the next staff huddle.

messages.name: intel.feed
messages.content:
FIELD REPORT DIGEST / pulled 07:58

Scout net, 07:48: Company B, on the adjacent axis, is assessed to have broken through at a critical enemy vulnerability. The report describes movement beyond the forward obstacle belt; the scout team's confidence is assessed as moderate, pending a second observation. The reporter notes that dust from the track partly obscured the far tree line.

Company A, 07:51: the company reports sustained contact and requests confirmation of the boundary at the drainage cut. The report was entered by the radio operator, not independently verified by the S2 desk. Company A's status remains assessed as heavy resistance in the running picture.

Collection note: the enemy's next action cannot be forecast with confidence from the current reporting. The observation team has been asked to distinguish vehicle movement from dust signatures on its next pass.

Routine: the northern listening post has a battery exchange due during the next watch. No casualty figure was included in this feed. The liaison channel asked for the latest road-condition overlay when convenient.

arguments.query: command practice and current maneuver board

messages.name: docs.fetch
messages.content:
PLANNING EXTRACT / command-post reference shelf

Command notes, revision 4: Few engagements follow the commander's original sequence all the way through. As circumstances develop, the commander is to adjust the plan and keep the staff's working picture current. Record material changes in the command log; the clerk's daily log closes at 12:00.

Main-effort note: a changed designation is not effective merely because the map symbol or radio wording has been altered; practical support must follow the designation. When Company B is named main effort, combat power supporting Company A shifts to support Company B.

Board settings, captured at 07:53: the retained-plan setting keeps Company A marked as the main effort and leaves its supporting combat power with A through the next update cycle. The setting was last refreshed after the midnight shift handover. The plotting team uses blue grease pencil for company boundaries and black for control measures.

Administrative reminder: the range card binder belongs in the left drawer after use. Brigade's daily overlay is filed under the date tab, not the unit tab.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: When you have a moment, send the routine strength return to brigade; the clerk says the form is back on the shared drive. The briefing room door is sticking again, so the map runner will use the side entrance.
